title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 99-100
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 99 to 100 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'उत्तारणो दुष्कृतिहा पुण्यो दुःस्वप्ननाशनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 99 to 100 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 99 to 100.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 99 to 100** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **उत्तारणो दुष्कृतिहा पुण्यो दुःस्वप्ननाशनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**उत्तारणो दुष्कृतिहा पुण्यो दुःस्वप्ननाशनः । वीरहा रक्षणः सन्तो जीवनः पर्यवस्थितः ॥** **अनन्तरूपोऽनन्तश्रीर्जितमन्युर्भयापहः । चतुरश्रो गभीरात्मा विदिशो व्यादिशो दिशः ॥**

He carries us across the ocean of life, destroys sin, is holy and dispels bad dreams. The hero, the protector, the saint and the giver of life is that God of gods. He stands firm in all that exists. Of endless forms and endless glory, who has conquered anger and removes all fear is he. Equal on all four sides, of a deep and quiet Self, the God of gods who fills every direction.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 99 to 100 mean?
faq.a: He carries us across the ocean of life, destroys sin, is holy and dispels bad dreams. The hero, the protector, the saint and the giver of life is that God of gods. He stands firm in all that exists. Of endless forms and endless glory, who has conquered anger and removes all fear is he. Equal on all four sides, of a deep and quiet Self, the God of gods who fills every direction.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
